summary: Stale pin consensus after regional migration with delayed rollback causes split fallback to mixed model variants
description: Issue summary: During a scheduled regional migration (eu-west -> eu-central) for Atlas Health's dedicated pool, a delayed rollback left stale pin consensus in the control plane. As a result, a subset of tenant sessions continued to carry an old model pin that no longer existed on the target shard. This produced mixed fallback behavior: some requests routed to the fallback variant (redwood-4b-v2-quant) while others were diverted to the new stable variant. Impact: partial correctness regressions for ~12% of requests (customer-reported hallucination rate increase), increased 5xx rate from 0.2% to 1.8% for the tenant, and visible latency spikes on affected cohorts. Environment: prod:eu-west (primary), eu-central-1 (target); Atlas Health dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool).
impact: Customer reports therapy-recommendation API returning inconsistent completions for identical prompts. Business impact: user-facing inconsistency for a subset of requests, elevated error budget burn and on-call engagement required.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Atlas Health tenant (tenant-id provided in private notes) on dedicated pool. 2) Trigger regional migration job with control-plane snapshot sync disabled (replica-merge path). 3) Initiate long-lived session flows (streaming chat + pinned model). 4) Force edge reconnects on ~10% of client sessions (simulated with client reconnect tool). 5) Observe mixed routing to two model variants and error spikes in the serving runtime.
logs: Edge proxy logs: repeated 409s when attempting to bind session pin; control-plane logs: snapshot-commit delayed by 37s due to merge conflict; serving-runtime: KV cache miss followed by fallback routing to quant variant. Sample log keys: cp.commit.id=aa7b3e2, edge.req=4762b1, sr.trace=ff12ab. Dashboards: /dashboards/tenant/atlas/rollout-routing, latency spike graph showed 120ms p95 -> 470ms p95 in window 2026-02-20T03:12:00Z.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: stale control-plane snapshot not applied to all edge shards before rollback window closed. Hypothesis B: edge shard cache TTL longer than expected combined with cookie domain change during migration resulted in session rebind to old shard. Reproducible in staging when disabling snapshot sync; cannot reproduce with normal snapshot flow. Correlated events: autoscaler activity at same time caused brief serving-runtime scale-down which prolonged commit.

2026-02-21 Priya Nair (SRE): Found edge cache TTL configured at 90s for this tenant, control-plane snapshot applied at 45s after commit — mismatch window allowed stale pins to persist.

2026-02-21 Customer (Atlas Health): We saw 13% of our requests return different model outputs for identical inputs between 03:10-03:20 UTC. This caused user confusion. Asking for confirmation that rollback was fully completed.
2026-02-22 Diego Morales: Mitigation applied: orchestrator forced snapshot re-sync to all edge shards, edge cache invalidation sent to affected regions; response normalization in transit.
2026-02-24 Support: Running regression tests on a canary group to confirm pin coherence; will schedule follow-up to tighten snapshot/TTL alignment and add invariant checks in control-plane.
2026-02-24 Aisha Patel: Marking follow-up tasks for product/infra: add pre-commit shard-coherence check, and alert on snapshot-commit >10s.
root_cause: Control-plane snapshot commit was delayed during regional migration while edge shard cache TTL remained high. This allowed pinned session tokens to reference a model variant that had been removed on the target shards, producing mixed fallback routing until a forced re-sync and cache invalidation were run.
resolution: Mitigation (2026-02-21): forced re-sync of control-plane snapshot to all edge shards, invalidated edge pin caches for Atlas tenant, restarted orchestrator commit walker. Long-term fix: add pre-migration TTL alignment check and enforce snapshot commit confirmation before migration window closes; add automated rollback guard to block migrations if any shard reports pending commits >5s.
postmortem_actions: 1) Infra: implement snapshot-coherence validation + alert (owner: Priya Nair). 2) Runtime: decrease default edge pin TTL from 90s to 15s for dedicated tenants (owner: Samir Chowdhury). 3) Product: update migration runbook to include forced pre-sync step and canary verification (owner: Diego Morales). 4) CS: notify Atlas Health of fixes and SLA remediation credit (owner: Aisha Patel).
